2607.25060.title: Lantern: Conflict-Aware Gradient Blending for Physics-Guided Diffusion Models in Calorimeter Simulation
2607.25060.paper_summary: Monte Carlo simulation of calorimeter showers is a principal bottleneck for the High-Luminosity LHC, and diffusion models have emerged as fast, high-fidelity surrogates. Their denoising objective is purely statistical, however: a model can minimize it while placing the physics wrong. Existing physics-informed generative methods cannot close this gap, because they assume a closed-form law, a governing PDE residual or a hard per-sample constraint, that a shower does not supply: no per-sample PDE governs a stochastic cascade, and energy conservation fixes only one scalar per shower. Standard metrics ignore the correlation structure across calorimeter layers and voxels, comparing showers only in a physics feature space. We address both gaps. We introduce the Correlation Frobenius Distance (CFD), a single normalized score for correlation fidelity at layer-wise and voxel-wise scales. We then encode the soft per-sample structure available in a shower as two physics-aware auxiliary losses: a variance-stabilized voxel residual loss grounded in counting statistics, and a graph Laplacian loss over the detector geometry. We combine both with denoising through GradBlend, which anchors the step magnitude to the denoising gradient while letting the auxiliary steer its direction, yielding Lantern, a physics-guided diffusion surrogate. On CaloChallenge Dataset 2, injecting the physics losses through task-symmetric rules such as PCGrad, GradNorm, IMTL-G, and ConFIG inflates FPD by 2-100x relative to denoising alone, whereas GradBlend admits the same signal without regression and, with the Laplacian loss, Lantern improves both FPD and CFD. Our ablation on the auxiliary loss scheduler shows that the voxel residual loss, whose gradient conflicts with denoising, requires a terminal denoising-only phase to preserve shower fidelity, whereas the non-conflicting Laplacian loss is insensitive to the schedule.
2607.25060.paper_summary_zh: 蒙特卡羅模擬熱量計淋浴是高亮度LHC的主要瓶頸，而擴散模型已成為快速、高保真的替代品。 然而，它們的去噪目標純粹是統計性的：一個模型可以最小化它，同時將物理學放錯。 現有的物理知識生成方法無法彌補這一差距，因為它們假設一個封閉形式的定律、一個控制的PDE殘差或一個硬的每樣本約束，而淋浴並不提供這些：沒有每樣本的PDE支配隨機級聯，而能量守恆僅固定每個淋浴的一個標量。 標準指標忽略了熱量計層和體素之間的相關結構，只在物理特徵空間中比較淋浴。 我們解決了這兩個差距。 我們引入了相關弗羅貝尼烏斯距離（CFD），這是一個單一的標準化分數，用於層級和體素級別的相關保真度。 然後，我們將淋浴中可用的軟每樣本結構編碼為兩個物理感知的輔助損失：一個基於計數統計的方差穩定體素殘差損失，以及一個在探測器幾何上進行的圖拉普拉斯損失。 我們將兩者與通過GradBlend的去噪結合，這將步驟大小固定在去噪梯度上，同時讓輔助引導其方向，產生了Lantern，一個物理引導的擴散替代品。 在CaloChallenge數據集2上，通過PCGrad、GradNorm、IMTL-G和ConFIG等任務對稱規則注入物理損失，使FPD相對於僅去噪增加了2-100倍，而GradBlend在不回歸的情況下接受相同的信號，並且通過拉普拉斯損失，Lantern同時改善了FPD和CFD。 我們對輔助損失調度器的消融研究顯示，體素殘差損失，其梯度與去噪相衝突，需要一個終端的僅去噪階段來保持淋浴的保真度，而不衝突的拉普拉斯損失對調度不敏感。
